finalists.label: Leukemia
finalists.why: It has the most specific and decisive evidence, including violaceous cutaneous lesions and a high white blood cell count with atypical cells/blasts.

finalists.label: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
finalists.why: It explains the severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, but lacks specific evidence like leukemia cutis.

finalists.label: Cauda Equina Syndrome
finalists.why: It accounts for the nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, but does not explain the systemic findings like leukemia cutis.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, a high white blood cell count with atypical cells/blasts, and the lack of alternative explanations for these findings in the runner-up made Leukemia the most compelling diagnosis.
